summary: Registering one host timer and capturing its handle gives constant JavaScript scheduling and cancellation overhead, matching the constant lower bound for returning any callable cancellation control.

optimality.argument: The function must perform at least one constant-time action to return a cancellation function. One setTimeout registration, one captured handle, and one clearTimeout call use O(1) JavaScript work, excluding the separately supplied function's runtime and the host-managed waiting interval.

replacement_checks.evidence: Returning a callable cancellation control requires at least constant work and storage.
The implementation creates one timer and one closure; cancellation clears exactly that timer handle without polling or iteration.
Cases cover cancellation before, after, and at the scheduled deadline, minimum and maximum legal delays, variadic forwarding, strings, and a defined zero result.
